vulnerability.title: Jenkins CLI reader thread skips handleClose on a corrupted stream, leaving HTTP CLI request threads waiting indefinitely (unauthenticated DoS)

fixed_releases.verified_content: The 2.541 release commit ea9c7278 has the SECURITY-3630 master commit efa18163 as an ancestor (git merge-base --is-ancestor exits 0) and the 2.528.3 release commit 40e29179 has the LTS commit 92b61576 as an ancestor. PlainCLIProtocol.java, CLIAction.java and FullDuplexHttpService.java are blobs 4bd45b7b, 4538d857 and 4b83d49d at both fix commits and at both release tags. In the fixed trees PlainCLIProtocol calls side.handleClose() from a finally, and both wait loops in CLIAction.run and FullDuplexHttpService.upload are bounded by CONNECTION_TIMEOUT. Security3630Test asserts that a full-duplex CLI connection whose stream is closed early releases its request thread within 2x CONNECTION_TIMEOUT.

severity.numeric_level_rationale: NVD publishes a single CVSS 3.1 metric, 7.5 HIGH, from the Secondary source (CISA-ADP); there is no Primary metric. OSV/GHSA repeats the same 7.5 vector and records HIGH, which is the same high band. The CNA container has no CVSS metric. Every published severity level is high, so the level is consistent and the score is not averaged.

vulnerability.category_l2: The PlainCLIProtocol reader calls side.handleClose() on every exit path except IOException, so a corrupted CLI stream ends the reader without waking the session; CLIAction.run and FullDuplexHttpService.upload then wait without a timeout and hold their request threads

description: Jenkins exposes the HTTP-based CLI at cli?remoting=false as a full-duplex pair of requests. FullDuplexHttpService.Response.generateResponse (2.441 lines 166-199) explicitly establishes the connection without any permission check (comment at 168-169: 'do not require any permission to establish a CLI connection'); the download request runs the CLI session while the upload request supplies the client's frames. On the server the frames are read by PlainCLIProtocol.run (2.441 lines 124-167). Its outer catch chain calls side.handleClose() for ClosedChannelException (156), ReadPendingException (162) and RuntimeException (165), but the IOException branch (157-158) only logs and returns. That is the branch taken when the stream is corrupted - for example the 'corrupt stream: negative frame length' IOException thrown at line 136, or any IOException raised by the socket - so a corrupted connection ends the reader without notifying the CLI session. The session's run() method blocks in CLIAction.java 274-279 on 'while (!ready) wait();'. ready is set by ready() (269-272) from onStart() (247-249), which fires only when the START frame has been parsed, and from handleClose() (261-267); a stream corrupted before that point therefore never wakes the command thread. The download request thread therefore parks forever, and because completed is set in the finally of that same run() (FullDuplexHttpService.java 118-124) the paired upload request also stays parked in FullDuplexHttpService.upload (2.441 lines 144-147, 'while (!completed) wait();'). CONNECTION_TIMEOUT (15 s, line 71) exists and is already applied to the download-side wait for the upload stream (104-116), but not to these two waits. An unauthenticated client can open such connections at will and corrupt the stream, pinning request-handling threads and their sockets indefinitely; repeating this exhausts the HTTP thread pool and denies service to legitimate users. The SECURITY-3630 fix (efa18163 master, 92b61576 LTS) moves side.handleClose() into a finally in PlainCLIProtocol, bounds both waits with CONNECTION_TIMEOUT in 1 s slices, makes CLIAction return early on timeout and FullDuplexHttpService.upload throw IOException('CLI timeout'), and replaces CLIAction's HashMap of pending duplex services with a ConcurrentHashMap (the concurrent-admission race is the second defect covered by the same commit). Security3630Test::testIndefiniteWait opens a CLI stream, writes 10 bytes, closes it, and asserts the 'Handling POST /jenkins/cli' thread disappears within 2x CONNECTION_TIMEOUT.

critical_operation.description: The IOException exit path - the one a corrupted stream takes - is the only one that does not call side.handleClose(), so the CLI session is never told the stream ended. The fix replaces the three per-branch calls with a single finally.

entry_point.description: Unauthenticated full-duplex request to cli?remoting=false: a download side with a Session header, then an upload side whose stream is corrupted and closed.

source_crosscheck.notes: The CNA, NVD, OSV and the GitHub advisory agree on the mechanism (HTTP-based CLI connections are not properly closed when the stream is corrupted, enabling unauthenticated denial of service) and on the fixed releases (2.541 weekly, 2.528.3 LTS). NVD publishes no Primary metric; its only metric is the CISA-ADP Secondary 7.5 HIGH, which OSV/GHSA repeats as HIGH, and the CNA has no metric, so all published levels are high. CWE-404 is recorded by NVD's Secondary source and by GHSA; the CNA lists none. The GHSA ECOSYSTEM weekly range introduced=2.529 conflicts with the CNA text and the CVE GIT range (introduced 0); this dataset follows the CNA and GIT range and records the conflict. The OSV record also links an independent Fluid Attacks write-up of the unauthenticated CLI DoS.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read PlainCLIProtocol at 2.441 and confirm the IOException branch does not call side.handleClose() while the other three branches do.
An independent reviewer must confirm that a corrupted stream reaches that IOException branch and that CLIAction.run and FullDuplexHttpService.upload then wait without a timeout.
An independent reviewer must confirm the fix commits efa18163/92b61576 move handleClose() into a finally and bound both waits, and that they are contained in releases 2.541 and 2.528.3.
An independent reviewer must confirm the affected range (weekly <=2.540, LTS <=2.528.2) and that 2.441 is inside it.
An independent reviewer must confirm all published severity levels are high (7.5) and record CWE-404.
An independent reviewer must confirm this entry is distinct from the other Jenkins CVEs in the dataset.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Static verification only; no Jenkins instance, HTTP request or test was run.

The DoS is modeled from the code paths: one corrupted connection parks the download and upload request threads indefinitely; exhausting the servlet container's thread pool requires many such connections, which this dossier does not exercise.

The CVE combines two defects fixed in one commit (the missing close/indefinite wait and the HashMap race in CLIAction); this dossier's location and claim cover the missing close, as named by the CVE description, and records the HashMap race in the description without claiming it as the location.
The GHSA ECOSYSTEM weekly range introduced=2.529 conflicts with the CNA and the CVE GIT range; the conflict is documented, not resolved silently.
No third-party reproduction or PoC was used; the Fluid Attacks write-up is cited by the OSV record but was not executed.
open_questions: Whether the servlet container's request thread is also released by connection-level timeouts in some deployments was not determined; the Jenkins fix bounds the wait regardless.
